headline: 305 of 406 materials carried userData.surfaceUniforms that no shader installed. Reproduced at HEAD, attributed to every call site, fixed at the copy seam, and now 0 of 406. Three further losses at the same seam were found and fixed with it.

the_population.the_player: 14 of the 16 materials on renderer.playerMesh were orphaned: skin, cloth, the three spine frills, all three equipment sets (reed / chitin / xanmeer), eyes, pupils, shield rim / face / inner / straps, weapon metal and weapon haft. The only PBR material on the player that kept its shader is the SHARED `mats.skin` original used by the brow horns and shoulder scales — i.e. the one that was never copied. The other two are MeshBasicMaterials (contact shadow, action silhouette) that never had the pass.
the_population.routes_checked: Material.copy() via .clone() is the only live route. There is no `new THREE.Material().copy(worldMat)` in game/src, no instancing route (InstancedMesh shares the material object), no LOD-generation route (the `lod` axis is a worldMaterial() option, not a copy), and the two material caches — province.js STYLE_MATERIAL_CACHE and kits.js MAT_CACHE — cache the RESULT of a clone and of worldMaterial() respectively, so the cache is not itself a route, it is what makes one clone serve many meshes.

the_four_losses_at_one_seam.A_bookkeeping: userData.surfaceUniforms SURVIVES the copy as a dead JSON ghost (uDetailNormal.value is no longer a Texture). 305 of 406 before, 0 after. THIS is why every static inspection said the material tables were fine: they were fine.
the_four_losses_at_one_seam.B_shader: onBeforeCompile is not copied. 305 before, 0 after.
the_four_losses_at_one_seam.C_wetness_driver: shadedMaterials.add() is not re-run, so setWorldWetness() could not reach the copy. 305 of 406 did not follow a sentinel value before; 0 after.
the_four_losses_at_one_seam.D_loud_fallback: registerFamilyMaterial() is not re-run, so MATERIAL_API §7's deliberately-loud magenta ASSET-LOAD-FAILED fallback could not stain a copy. Measured by firing the real failure path on the `cloth` family: 130 of 131 cloth materials were NOT stained before; 0 of 131 after. The loud fallback was 0.8% effective on that family.
the_four_losses_at_one_seam.E_hook_clobber: actor.js#installWaterline ASSIGNED onBeforeCompile rather than chaining, so restoring the pass at the copy seam alone would still have left the player's body broken. Fixed by chaining, same shape as installSurfaceShader.

the_fix.level: the copy, not the call sites
the_fix.why: There are a dozen .clone() sites across province.js, actor.js, renderer.js and scene.js. Re-installing at each is a dozen chances to miss one and it rots the first time somebody adds the thirteenth. Instead installSurfaceShader records a JSON-safe RECIPE in userData (which survives the copy exactly as the uniforms did), and every material worldMaterial() builds carries an own-property `clone` that rebuilds the shader, the wetness registration and the fallback registration on the copy — and re-installs itself on the copy, so a clone of a clone is covered.
the_fix.why_clone_and_not_copy: Material.prototype.clone() is `new this.constructor().copy(this)`. The `copy` that runs belongs to the NEW object, which is a stock material, so an instance-level `copy` override on the source is never consulted — a copy hook would have been INERT and would have looked exactly like a fix. `clone` is the method invoked on the source.
the_fix.api_amendment_owed: MATERIAL_API.md is frozen and I did not edit it. Two exports were ADDED (an addition is permitted by §9; documenting it is owed): `installCopySeam(mat)` and `adoptMaterialCopy(copy, source)`. §8's export table should gain both rows, and §4 should state that `.clone()` of a worldMaterial is now a supported operation that preserves the surface pass.
the_fix.reversal: node tools/visual/w1-30-copy-seam-patch.mjs --revert — the same script that applied it, so the reversal cannot drift from the change. It refuses to apply twice and refuses to run against moved anchors.

reconciliation_with_the_blind_fidelity_v.asked_by: orchestrator, after RI-VIS06 Protocol A returned 0/5 with 'surfaces are not shaded, they are filled'
reconciliation_with_the_blind_fidelity_v.answer: The orphaning is CONCENTRATED (100% of the player's copied materials, 76% of building materials, 0% of terrain/water/canopy) but the SYMPTOM is universal, by two different mechanisms. Population 1, the 305: the shader was absent. Population 2, the 101 intact: the shader is present but both of its variant axes are pinned at zero in the shipped build — terrain is `worldMaterial('mud',{vertexColors:true})` with no wear, and nothing ever calls setWorldWetness(). So the intact materials run the pass with wear=0 and wetness=0 and get a detail-normal blend only. 'Every surface reads as flat diffuse albedo' is therefore consistent with BOTH populations and does not require a second cause for the flatness — but it does for the AO, which is genuinely absent everywhere (see could_not_do #1).
reconciliation_with_the_blind_fidelity_v.falsifiable_prediction: After this fix, a re-judged blind comparison should show buildings improving most (kit materials carry real wear 0.2-0.9 with wearFrom:'geometry' and baked esCurvature, so they go from no wear at all to real geometric edge wear), the player improving modestly (micro-relief only, until the CHARACTER_SPECS wear wiring lands), and terrain and canopy NOT CHANGING AT ALL. If terrain and canopy are still called flat, that is a second cause and it is not this seam.
